summary: Stale socket binding after dock hotplug causes loss of access to internal APIs when switching from wired dock to office Wi-Fi
description: After undocking a Windows laptop from the corporate USB-C dock and moving to office Wi-Fi, the ZeroTrust agent remains bound to the previously active wired interface. Result is successful VPN tunnel shown as UP but traffic to internal services (git.internal.redwood, k8s-api.internal.redwood) either stalls or experiences repeated TLS timeouts. SSH sessions reset and internal API calls see long tail latencies. This appears related to stale socket/interface bindings at the OS or agent level rather than a full tunnel failure.
impact: Multiple engineers in the SF office report inability to reach internal git/k8s APIs for ~10-30 minutes after undocking. Work interrupts feature work and CI jobs. Estimated 4-6 engineers affected during incident window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Dock Windows laptop to USB-C dock (wired connection). ZeroTrust Agent establishes VPN and internal routes; confirm access to git.internal.redwood and k8s-api.internal.redwood.
2) Undock the laptop (hot unplug) and connect to corporate Wi-Fi (Corp-Enterprise).
3) Observe ZeroTrust agent status: tunnel shows UP in agent UI, no immediate disconnect. Attempt to curl internal API endpoints or git clone.
4) Observe TCP stalls, repeated TLS handshake failures, or SSH connection resets despite tunnel indicated as established. Reboot or agent restart restores normal connectivity.
5) Reproduce intermittently; not every undock results in failure — seems correlated with fast handoff and DHCP lease timing.
observed_behavior: Agent shows tunnel as UP. ipconfig /all shows new Wi-Fi adapter with correct DNS suffix but agent still lists previous Ethernet interface IP in local interface table. Socket connections from user-space continue to attempt using stale local source IP, leading to asymmetric routing and dropped return traffic. Restarting ZeroTrust agent or fully rebooting the laptop restores normal traffic.
expected_behavior: Agent should rebind sockets or re-establish local bind to the new Wi-Fi interface on network change events so application flows use current interface addresses. No packet loss or TLS timeout after undock/roam.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: DHCP/dns-suffix update not propagated to running sockets; agent's rebind logic does not handle hot unplug edge-case on Windows USB-C docks.
Reproduced on two Windows laptops (Surface Pro 9 and Lenovo X1) both running ZTA 2.3.1. No repro observed on Mac. Repro rate ~40% in local tests.
Packet capture shows outbound SYNs using stale Ethernet source IP after undock; replies routed to Wi-Fi and dropped by host (no matching conntrack entry for source IP).
Workaround observed: restarting ZTA or toggling airplane mode forces interface teardown and rebind, restoring connectivity without reboot.
Checked GPO/power settings: dock undock triggers interface down event but Windows sometimes delays removing Ethernet adapter entries from IP stack while Wi-Fi comes up, creating small overlap window.
No related kernel patches applied recently. ZeroTrust agent logs show attempted graceful rebind but error path returns 'EADDRINUSE' for existing sockets.
Related to agent rebind codepath: suspect missing SO_BINDTODEVICE or not re-binding ephemeral outbound sockets created by user apps; need dev input.
Priority: high for SF office mobility use-cases; blocking developer workflows.

Potential mitigation: ship a short agent update that forces unbind/close of ephemeral sockets on network-change events; longer-term: add aggressive interface takeover logic and Windows-specific handling for dock hotplug events.

resolution: Mitigation in progress: Agent Eng to ship hotfix (2.3.2) that forcibly closes and rebinds sockets on network-change for Windows. Patch PR created and under review.

Interim workaround: instruct affected users to restart the ZeroTrust agent or toggle airplane mode after undocking. On-site IT can also reconnect dock, then undock after agent restart to avoid stale bindings.
Post-incident follow-up: add automated telemetry to detect stale-binding occurrences and surface in Console; update runbook for dock hotplug scenarios.
